memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'When you sacrifice a thank offering to the LORD, sacrifice it in
such a way that it will be accepted on your behalf. It must be eaten
that same day; leave none of it till morning. I am the LORD'"
- Lev 22:29-30 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The thank offering had to be eaten the same day. Nothing kept back for
tomorrow, nothing stored away. This meant the worshipper could not
possibly eat it all alone. He had to invite others - family,
neighbours, the poor, the Levite. Gratitude to God became a shared meal
in the community.

What a beautiful arrangement. God designed thankfulness so that it
naturally overflowed into hospitality.

Dear reader, is that how your gratitude works? It is easy for
thankfulness to stay private, a warm feeling that never leaves our own
heart. God built it to spread.

The New Testament carries this forward. Hebrews calls us to continually
offer a sacrifice of praise - the fruit of lips that openly profess His
name - and then immediately adds: do not forget to do good and to share
with others, for with such sacrifices God is pleased (Heb 13:15-16).
Praise and generosity sit in the same sentence.

Notice also the urgency: eat it today. Do not delay gratitude. Do not
save thankfulness for a better season.

Whatever God has done for you this week, thank Him today - and let
someone else share in the joy of it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What has God done recently that I have not properly thanked Him for?
2. Does my gratitude stay private or spill over to others?
3. Who could I invite in and share God's goodness with this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You for kindnesses I have received without acknowledging.
Make my gratitude generous, and let it overflow to the people around
me. Amen.
